name: Does stablecoin supply growth lead prices

sections.hypothesis: Weeks that start while the total USD-pegged stablecoin supply is growing (above its level 4 weeks earlier) are followed by better BTC and ETH returns than weeks that start while it is shrinking.
sections.rationale: Who pays: new dollars enter crypto as stablecoins (USDT, USDC and others are minted on deposit), then buy coins; supply growth is fresh demand arriving, published daily. A long-only account could hold BTC or ETH only while new money is arriving. Outside evidence exists but is mixed: studies of Tether issuance and Bitcoin prices disagree on whether issuance leads prices or follows them (I'm citing from memory; this is why it's a raw-effect study first, not a strategy). It is not a variant of a rejected family: it reads money flows, not price patterns or sentiment. Suggested by Claude (2026-11-15) after the batch tests: the one untried idea with an economic reason that fits spot, long-only, weekly trading.
sections.rules: kestrel signal-study stablecoins BTCUSDT ETHUSDT. Each Sunday's daily close (UTC) is a sample; the signal is on when the supply known at the close (a day's figure counts from two days later, the conservative attention rule) is above its value 28 days before that. Outcome: the log return to the next Sunday's close. Samples a week apart never overlap; BTC and ETH are pooled. Daily bars from 2018-01 (the supply history starts 2017-11-29) to 2025-10, never the holdout. Run once.
sections.falsification: PROCEED only if P(spread > 0) is at least 90% (bootstrap) and the spread (mean week after growth minus mean week after shrinkage) beats one round trip of costs; otherwise KILL. The result also reports how often the past week rose when the signal was on: if growth only follows rising prices, it is momentum under another name, and that is said plainly. A PROCEED leads to a strategy note, judged on the full scorecard; a KILL ends it.
sections.parameters: None to choose: 28 days (4 weeks) and the two-day lag are fixed here, as in the attention and news-tone studies.
sections.costs: A study, not a strategy: one look, recorded with the study's verdict. The hurdle is one round trip at kestrel.toml's costs (about 22 bps). Caveat: DefiLlama's history is its reconstruction today, not what was published at the time.

history.reason: PROCEED (spread +1.17% a week, P 91%); the stablecoin hold is on watch. Cleanup (Luke, 2026-11-15).
